identity_evidence: Wikisource 'Executive Order 351-B (1905)', signed Sept. 18, 1905, approving Acting Secretary of War's recommendation of Sept. 15, 1905; Fort San Pedro, Iloilo, Panay
basis: The order alters the military reservation at Fort San Pedro in the Philippine Islands under section 12 of the Philippine Government Act of 1902. Its reservation of Philippine public lands rested on U.S. sovereignty and had no object after Philippine independence on July 4, 1946. Nothing in the text points to property the United States kept after 1946.

identity_evidence: Wikisource 'Executive Order 602 (1907)', signed March 28, 1907; calls election for Philippine Assembly
basis: The order directs the Philippine Commission to call a general election for the Philippine Assembly under the Philippine Government Act of 1902. This concerns the insular legislative administration of the Islands under U.S. sovereignty. It was a one-time command and the insular structure ended at the Commonwealth's inauguration.

notes: A later outer bound of 1946-07-04 also holds. The rule card's earlier date was chosen because the order concerns the Commission and insular government, not only U.S. sovereignty.
